en: I have an exam tomorrow, so I am studying tonight.
tamil: நாளைக்கு எனக்கு பரீட்சை இருக்கு, அதனால இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி படிச்சிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a friend why you cannot go out.
explain: 'So' joins a reason with its result. 'Am studying' shows an action happening now.
usage: Use it with friends when you must refuse an invitation because of studies.
leelaQ: Do you study at night or in the morning?
answer: I study at night because the house is quiet.

en: When does your exam start?
tamil: உன் பரீட்சை எப்போ ஆரம்பிக்கும்?
context: Asking a friend about the exam date.
explain: A 'When' question asks for the time. The helper 'does' comes before the subject.
usage: Use it with a classmate when you plan your own preparation.
leelaQ: What is the first exam on your timetable?
answer: The first exam is English on Monday.

en: Our teacher explained the lesson very clearly.
tamil: எங்க டீச்சர் பாடத்தை ரொம்ப தெளிவா விளக்கினாங்க.
context: Praising a teacher to a classmate.
explain: 'Explained' is the past of explain. 'Very clearly' adds strength to the praise.
usage: Say it to classmates or parents when a teacher teaches well.
leelaQ: Who is your favourite teacher and why?
answer: My favourite teacher is my maths sir because he explains everything slowly.

en: Please open your books to page twenty.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு உங்க புத்தகத்தை இருபதாம் பக்கத்துல திறங்க.
context: A teacher starting the lesson.
explain: 'Please' makes an order polite. 'Open to page' is a classroom phrase.
usage: Teachers use it to start the lesson politely.
leelaQ: What do you say to start a class?
answer: I say good morning and ask everyone to open the book.

en: I will finish my homework before dinner.
tamil: நான் சாப்பாட்டுக்கு முன்னாடி என் ஹோம்வொர்க்கை முடிச்சிடுவேன்.
context: Promising a parent you will complete homework.
explain: 'Will' shows a promise about the future. 'Before dinner' gives the time limit.
usage: Use it with your mother or father when they ask about your homework.
leelaQ: When do you usually do your homework?
answer: I usually do my homework after I come back from school.

en: I did not understand the last chapter at first.
tamil: கடைசி பாடம் முதல்ல எனக்கு புரியல.
context: Telling a teacher honestly.
explain: 'Did not' + base verb makes a past negative. 'At first' means in the beginning.
usage: Use it when you tell a teacher where you had trouble.
leelaQ: What was difficult for you at first, but easy later?
answer: Driving was difficult at first, but now it is easy.

en: Did you finish the homework?
tamil: நீ ஹோம்வொர்க்கை முடிச்சிட்டியா?
context: Asking a classmate before class.
explain: 'Did' makes a past question. The main verb goes back to the base form.
usage: Use it with classmates before the teacher checks the notebooks.
leelaQ: Do you finish your work on time?
answer: Yes, I try to finish my work before the deadline.

en: She has completed her engineering degree.
tamil: அவ இன்ஜினியரிங் டிகிரியை முடிச்சிருக்கா.
context: Telling someone about a cousin's studies.
explain: 'Has completed' tells about a finished action with a result that matters now.
usage: Use it when you talk about a relative's education in a family chat.
leelaQ: What degree did you study?
answer: I studied commerce at a college in Madurai.

en: The class starts at nine every morning.
tamil: கிளாஸ் தினமும் காலையில ஒன்பது மணிக்கு ஆரம்பிக்கும்.
context: Telling a new student the timing.
explain: Simple present is used for daily routines and fixed timings.
usage: Use it to tell a new student or a parent the class timing.
leelaQ: What time does your class or work start?
answer: My work starts at ten in the morning.

en: Which subject do you find most difficult?
tamil: எந்த பாடம் உனக்கு ரொம்ப கஷ்டமா இருக்கு?
context: Chatting with a new friend.
explain: 'Which' is used when you choose from a limited group. 'Find' means think of it as.
usage: Use it to start a study chat with a classmate.
leelaQ: Why is that subject difficult for you?
answer: It is difficult because there are too many formulas.

en: Could you lend me your notes for a day?
tamil: உன் நோட்ஸை ஒரு நாளைக்கு எனக்கு கொடுக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking a classmate.
explain: 'Could you' is softer and more polite than 'can you'. 'Lend' means give for a short time.
usage: Use it with a classmate when you missed a class.
leelaQ: Do you lend your things easily to others?
answer: Yes, I lend my notes to my close friends.

en: I am preparing for the NEET exam this year.
tamil: நான் இந்த வருஷம் நீட் தேர்வுக்கு தயாராகிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a relative about your exam plans.
explain: 'Am preparing' shows an effort that is going on for some time, not only right now.
usage: Use it when relatives or neighbours ask what you are doing after school.
leelaQ: What exam are you preparing for?
answer: I am preparing for the bank exam.

en: We submitted the project report yesterday.
tamil: நாங்க நேத்து ப்ராஜெக்ட் ரிப்போர்ட்டை சமர்ப்பிச்சோம்.
context: Telling a friend the project is done.
explain: 'Submitted' is the past form. 'Yesterday' tells the exact time.
usage: Use it with classmates or a guide when asked about your project status.
leelaQ: Have you ever done a college project?
answer: Yes, I made a small billing software for my final year.

en: Have you submitted the assignment yet?
tamil: நீ அசைன்மென்ட்டை இன்னும் சப்மிட் பண்ணலயா?
context: Checking with a classmate.
explain: 'Yet' is used in questions about something expected. 'Have you' begins the question.
usage: Use it when the deadline is near and you want to check with a friend.
leelaQ: When is your next deadline?
answer: My next deadline is on Friday.

en: Revising a little every day works better than studying all night.
tamil: ஒவ்வொரு நாளும் கொஞ்சம் கொஞ்சமா திருப்பி படிக்கிறது ராத்திரி முழுக்க படிக்கிறதை விட நல்லா வேலை செய்யும்.
context: Giving a study tip to a junior.
explain: 'Revising' works as the subject. 'Better than' compares two study methods.
usage: Use it when you advise a younger student about exam preparation.
leelaQ: What is your best study tip?
answer: My best tip is to revise a little every day.

en: Don't copy from your friend's answer sheet.
tamil: உன் நண்பனோட விடைத்தாள்ல இருந்து காப்பி அடிக்காத.
context: Warning a classmate.
explain: 'Don't' + verb is a negative command. Copying in an exam is wrong.
usage: Use it as advice with a younger sibling or a friend during an exam.
leelaQ: Why is honesty important in exams?
answer: Honesty is important because marks should show real effort.

en: Please explain the last point once more, madam.
tamil: மேடம், கடைசி பாயிண்டை இன்னொரு தடவை விளக்குங்க, தயவுசெஞ்சு.
context: Asking a teacher politely.
explain: Adding 'madam' or 'sir' shows respect. 'Once more' asks for a repeat.
usage: Use it with a teacher when you do not follow something in class.
leelaQ: How do you ask a teacher for help?
answer: I raise my hand and ask politely.

en: I should practise English speaking daily.
tamil: நான் தினமும் இங்கிலீஷ் பேசி பழகணும்.
context: Telling yourself or a friend about a goal.
explain: 'Should' gives advice or a duty. Note: the verb is 'practise' in British spelling.
usage: Use it when you talk about your learning goals with a friend or teacher.
leelaQ: How do you practise your English every day?
answer: I speak with my friends and watch English videos.

en: Which college are you planning to join?
tamil: நீ எந்த காலேஜ்ல சேரப் போற?
context: Asking a neighbour's child.
explain: 'Planning to' + verb talks about a plan. 'Which' offers a choice.
usage: Use it with a school leaver or their parents after the results.
leelaQ: What kind of college would you like to join?
answer: I would like a college with good teachers.

en: My brother is joining a college in Coimbatore next month.
tamil: என் தம்பி அடுத்த மாசம் கோயம்புத்தூர்ல ஒரு காலேஜ்ல சேரப் போறான்.
context: Sharing family news with a neighbour.
explain: 'Is joining' with 'next month' talks about a fixed plan in the near future.
usage: Use it with neighbours or colleagues when you share a family update.
leelaQ: Which college or school did you go to?
answer: I went to a government school near my house.

en: The professor gave us a new assignment today.
tamil: ப்ரொபசர் இன்னைக்கு எங்களுக்கு புது அசைன்மென்ட் கொடுத்தாரு.
context: Telling a roommate about college work.
explain: 'Gave' is the past of give. 'Us' is the person who receives.
usage: Use it with hostel mates or friends when you complain about workload.
leelaQ: Do you like getting assignments?
answer: Not really, but they help me learn the topic well.

en: Will the teacher give us extra time?
tamil: டீச்சர் நமக்கு கூடுதல் நேரம் தருவாங்களா?
context: Asking a classmate in the exam hall.
explain: 'Will' starts a question about the future. 'Extra time' means more than the fixed time.
usage: Use it with classmates when a test looks too long.
leelaQ: What do you do when you run out of time?
answer: I write the short answers first and then the long ones.

en: I have already revised the first three chapters.
tamil: நான் முதல் மூணு பாடத்தை ஏற்கனவே திருப்பி படிச்சிட்டேன்.
context: Telling a friend about your progress.
explain: 'Already' goes between 'have' and the main verb. It shows the work is done earlier than expected.
usage: Use it when a friend asks how far your exam preparation has gone.
leelaQ: How much of your work have you finished today?
answer: I have finished half of my work today.

en: Sit down quietly and complete the exercise.
tamil: அமைதியா உட்கார்ந்து பயிற்சியை முடிங்க.
context: A teacher instructing students.
explain: Two commands are joined by 'and'. 'Quietly' tells how to sit.
usage: Use it as a teacher or a tutor with a group of children.
leelaQ: What helps you stay calm in class?
answer: Sitting near the front helps me stay calm.

en: Our school reopens after the summer holidays on Monday.
tamil: கோடை விடுமுறைக்கு அப்புறம் எங்க ஸ்கூல் திங்கள்கிழமை திறக்கும்.
context: Telling a parent the reopening day.
explain: Simple present is used for official schedules, like school dates.
usage: Use it with parents or neighbours when they ask about the school calendar.
leelaQ: What do you do during the summer holidays?
answer: I visit my grandparents in my native village.
